rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A coordinated set of clauses functioning as a condition must be parsed jointly; its parts form one grammatical whole, just as both parts of a predicate, adjective, or circumstantial phrase do.
rows.anchor: فكما يكون الخبر والصفة والحال لا محالة في مجموع الجزءين لا في أحدهما كذلك يكون الشرط في مجموع الجملتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 4:112, the consequence of bearing slander and manifest sin follows from the combined act of acquiring an offense and then imputing it to an innocent person.
rows.anchor: الشرط كما لا يخفى في مجموع الجملتين لا في كل واحدة منهما على الانفراد

words: ومن يخرج من بيته مهاجرا إلى الله ورسوله ثم يدركه الموت
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of reward in 4:100 is attached to emigration together with death overtaking the emigrant while on that path, not to emigration alone.
rows.anchor: لم يعلق الحكم فيه بالهجرة على الانفراد

words: وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses about not being at the western side through the passage of time form one unit, coordinated with the unit about not residing in Midian and God’s sending; a flat clause-by-clause reading wrongly puts the latter under لكن.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أن يكون عطف مجموع

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari reports that al-Kindi called three forms redundant; Abu al-Abbas answered that they respectively assert, answer a question, and answer a denial, so their meanings differ.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن الأنباري أنه قال : ركب الكندي المتفلسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle إن binds the following clause to what precedes so the two cohere as one utterance; removing it makes them separate, and فاء does not restore the same relation.
rows.anchor: الجملة إذا هي دخلت ترتبط بما قبلها

rows.speaker: بشار
rows.claim: Bashshar’s line about starting early uses إن to show how the second clause becomes closely integrated with the first.
rows.anchor: في بيت بشار : ( بكرا صاحبي قبل الهجير إن ذاك النجاح في التبكير )

rows.speaker: بعض العرب
rows.claim: An anonymous Arab’s line about camel-song supplies a second poetic example of إن joining the clauses into a cohesive statement.
rows.anchor: من قول بعض العرب : ( فغنها وهي لك الفداء إن غناء الإبل الحداء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rhetorical merit belongs to the form in which meaning is expressed, not to bare words as sounds; descriptions such as elegance or ornament name qualities of that form and its effect on meaning.
rows.anchor: نسبوا ما كان من الحسن والمزية في صورة المعنى إلى اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A counted noun can be omitted after a numeral when it is understood; with one and two, however, the omitted noun must be an adjective, since Arabic does not use the corresponding singular or dual noun in an iḍāfa construction.
rows.anchor: ثم لا تستطيع أن تقدره إلا موصوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the cited rajaz line anomalous because it uses ثنتا with an expressed counted noun, unlike the regular one-and-two construction he describes.
rows.anchor: ظرف عجوز فيه ثنتا حنظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows the ellipsis ولا تقولوا ثلاثة آلهة, which denies gods’ existence; the alternative ولا تقولوا آلهتنا ثلاثة would deny only that their number is three.
rows.anchor: ولا تقولوا لنا أو في الوجود آلهة ثلاثة أو ثلاثة آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that denying three princes could still allow two does not fit this case: saying آلهتنا already presupposes the existence of gods, which the author rejects.
rows.anchor: قولهم آلهتنا : يوجب ثبوت آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding an object changes a transitive verb’s meaning rather than appending a separate fact; the object shapes what action is asserted, as an adjective shapes a noun’s reference.
rows.anchor: أنهم قد أصلوا في المفعول وكل ما زاد على جزءي الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These conditional examples can repeat a verb because its second use has a different meaning through its added complement; the condition and consequence therefore remain distinct rather than tautological.
rows.anchor: الشرط ينبغي أن يكون غير الجزاء من حيث كان الشرط سببا والجزاء مسببا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proverb about a person’s speech and courage, and the example إن أتاك زيد أتاك لحاجة, illustrate how the second verb can acquire a distinct sense through its added qualification or object.
rows.anchor: المرء بأصغريه إن قال قال ببيان وإن صال صال بجنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling eloquence a special arrangement of words is too general to explain it; one must specify the concrete features that distinguish correct from faulty expression and levels of excellence, as with brocade weaving.
rows.anchor: فكان يكفي في معرفة نسج الديباج الكثير التصاوير أن تعلم أنه ترتيب للغزل على وجه مخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an omitted noun or verb is correctly recoverable, its omission is often better and more natural than saying it explicitly; the suppressed element should be restored only where the context calls for it.
rows.anchor: وأنت تجد حذفه هناك أحسن من ذكره

rows.speaker: سمية
rows.claim: In the fragment attributed to Sumayya, the author supplies the omitted sense as ‘that is delusion I keep returning to, so leave off blaming me.’
rows.anchor: قالت سمية : قد غويت ، بأن رأت حقا تناوب مالنا ووفودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With أضحك وأبكى, أمات وأحيا, and أغنى وأقنى, the objects are omitted so the verbs assert God as the source of laughter and tears, life and death, and enrichment and contentment generally, without specifying an object.
rows.anchor: هو الذي منه الإحياء والإماتة والإغناء والإقناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both Zayd similes share the basic comparison, but كأن زيدا الأسد adds that he is so brave he is virtually indistinguishable from a lion; this extra nuance comes from the ordering and combination of the words.
rows.anchor: وإنما هو زيادة فيه وفي حكم الخصوصية في الشكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reporting that a seemingly harmless man killed someone, placing the killer first highlights the surprising fact that this unlikely agent acted; the novelty lies in who killed, not who was killed.
rows.anchor: ذاك لأن الذي يعنيه ويعني الناس من شأن هذا القتل طرافته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is insufficient to say an element was fronted for emphasis; the analyst must explain why it matters. Neglecting such rhetorical distinctions obscures eloquence and inimitability, unlike focusing only on sound details such as أأنذرتهم, imāla, and الصراط/الزراط.
rows.anchor: وقد وقع في ظنون الناس أنه يكفي أن يقال : إنه قدم للعناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With لم يأتني القوم كلهم, the negative applies to the whole group, so some may have come; with كلهم لم يأتني, it applies to each one, making the claim that some came contradictory.
rows.anchor: لم يأتني القوم كلهم ، ولكن أتاني بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The semantic difference does not truly arise from whether كل is governed by the verb; it arises from whether كل falls within the scope of negation, as the separable negator ما shows.
rows.anchor: وهو دخول كل في حيز النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two cited poems, ما كل ما يتمنى المرء يدركه and ما كل رأي الفتى يدعو إلى رشد, illustrate that كل remains within negation even when not governed by the verb; fronting كل outside negation instead denies any instance.
rows.anchor: ما كل رأي الفتى يدعو إلى رشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase’s rhetorical merit lies in the added nuance its arrangement creates: كأن زيدا الأسد conveys a stronger comparison than زيد كالأسد, as if Zayd’s bravery made him indistinguishable from a lion.
rows.anchor: وإذا لم يكن إلى الشك سبيل أن ذلك كان بالنظم فاجعله العبرة في الكلام كله
